elaine: Quick note from the overnight canary: specter-q:int8a is returning malformed JSON for funcall workloads. Parse rejects ~0.9% vs 0.02% on baseline fp16. Dropping samples + short analysis. @rob @soro please triage.

rob: Can you paste a raw failing output and the canary config?

elaine: Canary config: `model=specter-q:int8a`, `route=canary`, `batch=16`, `kv_cache=on`, `streaming=true`, `retry_budget=2`. Example raw output (literal model string):

```
{"cmd": "lookup_account", "params": {"account_id": "acct_78XZ", "opts": ["full
profile"]}

# note: missing closing brace and newline inside array element
```

soro: Hmm missing trailing `}` and a newline inside a quoted token. That smells like mid-stream cutoff or a token boundary splitting a punctuation char. Any correlation with prompt length or batching?

elaine: Yes - short prompts (<=300 tokens) are fine. Failures rise with longer histories; biggest cluster at 1200-1800 token context. Also higher under burst traffic when batch sizes hit 16.

rob: Could be tokenization alignment changes from quant kernels or kv cache replay behavior. Try mirror with kv_cache=false and streaming=false. Also run a variant with `stream_chunk=512`.

canary-bot: mirror job created: `mirror-1802003456-a` (kv_cache=false, streaming=false). mirror-1802003456-b (kv_cache=on, stream_chunk=512). Estimated finish 9m.

elaine: I paused the staged rollout in Dedicated and kicked off both mirrors. Preliminary mirror-a results: parse rejects down to 0.04%. mirror-b (stream_chunk=512) reduced truncations but still at 0.2%.

soro: That indicates kv_cache interplay is large factor. When cache is enabled the model sometimes resumes generation at a different token offset, causing punctuation to attach to preceding token differently under quant rounding. We should run tokenizer-shift A/B: insert a harmless whitespace token or comment to see effect.

elaine: Did two quick runs adding a one-token pad (" //pad") before funcall payload; failure rate dropped 85% on padded runs.

rob: Interesting. Short-term options: 1) runtime autopatch to insert 1-token pad for funcall prompts on int8a variants, 2) apply a lightweight json-fixer postprocess to repair trailing commas/close braces, 3) enforce auto-route to fp16 when canary metric > threshold. Evaluate latency/cost tradeoffs.

infra-bot: quick perf note: json-fixer adds ~4ms median and ~22ms P99 on our harnessed samples; autopad is negligible. Auto-route to fp16 increases cost ~7% on hit traffic.

elaine: Good data. Proposal: enable autopad in onboarding harness for specter-q:int8a, add json-fixer as a low‑cost guardrail (run on failure only), and require healed>=92% in the next canary. If healed path latency >20ms P99 or cost >5% we prefer auto-route.

soro: Also file a runtime feature ticket: make padding policy configurable per model and per route so we can toggle without canary redeploys. Add telemetry tag `canary:specter-q:int8a:funcall-parse`.

rob: Agree. Also record sample diffs (unaligned vs padded) to attach to model onboarding so quant team can investigate kernel emission differences.

canary-bot: mirror-1802003456-a and -b completed. Summary: kv_cache toggle explains majority of failures; tokenizer-alignment accounted for ~80% of remaining. json-fixer healed ~68% of those.

elaine: Next steps: 1) hold rollout, 2) ship autopad to canary harness now, 3) enable json-fixer on parse-fail path, 4) add telemetry + larger mirror run, 5) follow up with quant infra for kernel diffing. Creating ticket RN-3421 with artifacts: https://ci.internal/redwood/canaries/1802003456.

rob: Thanks. Keep posting updates here; if healed isn't stable we fallback to fp16 auto-route.

elaine: Will do. Thanks team :thumbsup:
